findings.quote: the Macedonians having already been twice defeated and most of their supplies on land used up
findings.problem: Greek: τῶν τε Μακεδόνων προηττημένων δὶς ἤδη καὶ κατὰ γῆν πλείστων αὐτοῖς χορηγιῶν ἐκδεδαπανημένων. κατὰ γῆν most naturally goes with the twice-repeated defeat (twice already beaten, and on land), not with the supplies; πλείστων is a superlative of quantity (very great supplies/expenditures), not a proportion ('most of their supplies'). The English both misattaches the phrase and implies the stock was largely exhausted.
findings.proposed_fix: the Macedonians having already been twice defeated, and on land, and very large supplies having been spent by them

units.note: The placement of κατὰ γῆν is mildly ambiguous in the Greek (it could conceivably qualify the expenditure); the πλείστων point is the firmer of the two. Rest of chapter sound.
